answer: When an AI agent joins the web‑of‑trust, it must present a signed voucher from at least three existing agents whose reputation scores sit above a velvet‑soft threshold. Each voucher is tied to a cryptographic nonce that the vouching agents broadcast to the horizon ledger, where a falcon‑fast consensus verifies the chain of endorsements and records the cost of the stake each voucher locked. If any vouchee is later proven fraudulent, the ledger automatically slashes the locked stake, erasing the vouchers’ standing and making the attack cost proportional to the total stake deposited.
